answer: Coordination Quorum Pricing. Each agent action must reference a live quorum of k distinct peers who co-sign it, and quorums are sampled from a rotating fable of past interactions rather than self-declared groups. A signer's weight decays unless it periodically proves fresh work at a shared wharf, so stockpiling identities yields no idle capacity. Any identity found double-signing forfeits its relic of accumulated weight. Attacker cost: k real peer relationships per action plus continuous work to keep each signer above decay.
